findings.evidence: console.warn(`⚠️ Không lấy được tên Facebook của ${senderId}: ${e?.message || err.message}`);
findings.explanation: senderId (the customer's raw Facebook PSID) is interpolated straight into a console.warn call with no hashing/redaction. Everywhere else in the codebase (core/webhook.js, core/utils/log-refs.js) sender/page IDs are passed through pageRef()/shopRef() which SHA-256-hash and truncate the ID before it hits the logs, and core/event-tracker.js's redactSensitiveText/redactEventMeta scrub PII before storage. This call site bypasses that pattern entirely, so a persistent customer identifier ends up verbatim in server logs whenever a Facebook profile-name lookup fails (e.g. rate limiting or an invalid/expired page token), which is a realistic and frequent path. No token or phone/email is exposed here, but it is an inconsistent redaction gap for a PII-grade identifier in the exact codepath (notification service invoked from webhook.js's operational alerting) the audit item targets.
